neighboring_unit_entries.title: Eta continuation suggests a fractional strip translated by alpha
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Uses the differing convergence domains of eta^(alpha) and zeta^(alpha) to define (alpha,1+alpha) as a translated counterpart of the critical strip and makes explicit that invariance of zero properties under that translation is only a possible scenario.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Factor the reflection equation so only one generalized-Leibniz sum remains
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Packages gamma, reflected zeta, and the elementary exponential into one function, proves the fractional derivative of the exponential factor, and states the single-series functional equation.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: The Caputo-style definition gives the desired Dirichlet coefficients but is awkward on products; switching to a Grunwald-Letnikov derivative restores a generalized Leibniz rule, after which exponential factorization reduces the functional equation from three sums to one and a trigonometric form.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: Fractional derivatives are nonunique, so these identities are tied to the chosen operator and complex-power conventions rather than canonical properties of every fractional calculus.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Operator choice controls whether symmetry is computationally expressible

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The known integer-derivative functional equation is reorganized into a coefficient-and-product template so that gamma, zeta, exponential, and trigonometric factors can later be fractionalized without carrying three independent infinite expansions.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The unit states Spira-Apostol formulas for the kth derivative under s↔1-s, involving finite sums of constants, trigonometric factors, gamma derivatives, and zeta derivatives. Replacing s by 1-s gives the comparison form used for the later fractional result.
directed.conceptual_reading: Choosing the right algebraic factorization is a computational simplification: shared exponential structure can be combined before generalized Leibniz expansion, reducing redundant summation channels.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The integer-order reflection formula is the bridge and calibration target for the proposed noninteger functional equation.
directed.boundary_or_failure: This span contains the integer template only; it neither proves the fractional coefficients nor establishes analytic or zero-theoretic consequences.
